summary:
Earth Mission Control: The 20-Minute Decision is an interactive browser-based Mars mission-control simulation developed to demonstrate the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars.

What we developed: We created a 2D interactive game in which players act as Earth-based mission controllers responsible for the survival of four astronauts at a fictional Mars outpost. Players investigate a previous outpost failure, analyze clues, identify the root cause, and respond to a new emergency involving solar power, oxygen, food, water, and radiation protection.

How it addresses the challenge: The game uses real NASA Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) dust-opacity observations to drive its dust and solar-power mechanics. It also simulates Earth–Mars communication delays, showing how commands cannot reach astronauts instantly and why mission controllers must plan ahead using limited resources and scientific information.

Why it is important: Future human missions to Mars will face communication delays, dust storms, power limitations, and life-support risks. This simulation turns these complex challenges into an interactive learning experience, helping players understand the importance of scientific data, resource management, teamwork, and critical decision-making in future space exploration.
details:
EARTH MISSION CONTROL: The 20-Minute Decision

What does it do?
An interactive Mars simulation where players investigate system failures and manage an emergency to protect four astronauts.

Benefits and intended impact:
Helps players understand Mars exploration challenges, resource management, communication delays, and astronaut safety.

Tools used:
HTML, CSS, JavaScript, NASA Curiosity dust-opacity data, GitHub Pages, OBS Studio, and Clipchamp.

Creativity:
Combines real NASA data with an interactive mission-control game involving investigations and time-sensitive decisions.

Factors considered:
Scientific accuracy, NASA data, communication delays, limited resources, astronaut safety, and user experience.
dataRefs: NASA Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) Mastcam 880 nm Optical Depth Dataset This dataset provides real Martian dust-opacity observations used in our game's dust and solar-power mechanics.
